raw_graphql_pull_request.body: # [AMD][Kimi-K3]: skip the routed_input copy when aiter reads the front slice as-is ## Motivation On ROCm, each Kimi-K3 MoE layer copies a strided view of the front GEMM output into a dense buffer before the experts, even though aiter's A8W4 kernels already read that view in place. This pull request skips that copy when the slice is 16-byte aligned, saving about 0.3–0.4 ms of decode time per token on MI355X while leaving every other backend unchanged. More specifically, `KimiK3MoE._forward_fused` reads `hidden_states` once through the merged front weight and splits the result into `[gate_up | router_logits | routed_input]`, so `routed_input` is a **strided view** into the front GEMM's output. Today that view is unconditionally repaired into a dense buffer before it reaches the experts: ```python if self._moe_front_needs_dense_bf16: routed_input = routed_input.to(hidden_states.dtype).contiguous() ``` `_moe_front_needs_dense_bf16` only clears for the SM100 trtllm-gen mxfp4 runner, so ROCm always takes it. The front is already bf16 on HIP (`_front_fp32` is `not _is_hip and ...`), which makes the `.to()` a no-op and leaves `.contiguous()` as a pure `[num_tokens, moe_hidden_size]` device-to-device copy — once per MoE layer, per forward. That copy is not needed under aiter's A8W4 activation mode (`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4`), which is the MoE configuration Kimi-K3 is most commonly served with on ROCm. There, `moe_runner/aiter.py` → `aiter.fused_moe` quantizes through `fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort`, and both kernels behind that entry address rows via `input.stride(-2)`, with only a same-shape `view(-1, N)` in between — so aiter consumes the strided slice directly. ## Modifications Adds `KimiK3MoE._aiter_takes_front_slice`, a cached property that is true exactly when aiter reads the routed rows as the front GEMM hands them over. It requires all of: - ROCm, `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4`, `Mxfp4MoEMethod`, aiter runner backend, and `method.hidden_size == self.moe_hidden_size` - `sum(self._front_sizes) % 8 == 0` **and** `sum(self._front_sizes[:-1]) % 8 == 0` — aiter's `fused_mx_quant_moe_sort_kernel` vector-loads 16 B from each row start, so both the front row pitch and the slice's own base offset into it must be 8 bf16-element aligned The activation mode matters because only A8W4 is stride-aware end to end: a16w4 re-densifies inside the FlyDSL stage-1 port, and A4W4 hands the slice to a stage1 that takes no stride. Both keep the copy. A8W4 also wins over `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` when both are set, matching aiter's own precedence. Gating on it is narrow in code but not in practice — it is the mode the ROCm Kimi-K3 serving configuration normally runs. The hot-path change is one added conjunct: ```python # False off ROCm, so this only ever widens the HIP path if self._moe_front_needs_dense_bf16 and not self._aiter_takes_front_slice: routed_input = routed_input.to(hidden_states.dtype).contiguous() ``` `_aiter_takes_front_slice` is `False` off ROCm and under every other activation mode, so every other backend is bit-for-bit unchanged. The property is also added to the cache-invalidation list in `_merge_front_weights`, since it depends on `_front_sizes`. Single file: `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`. ## Accuracy Tests The strided view and the contiguous copy hold identical values, and aiter's quant kernel reads the same rows either way — this is a memory-layout change, not a numerics change. `lm_eval` gsm8k, 5-shot, full set (1319 questions), 64 concurrent, MI355X / ROCm 7.2.4 / SGLang 0.5.20: | Filter | Base | Strided | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | flexible-extract | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 0.9621 ± 0.0053 | -0.0061 | | strict-match | 0.9674 ± 0.0049 | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | -0.0061 | Both deltas are inside run-to-run noise — about 0.85σ on the standard error of the difference, or 8 questions out of 1319. Decode results are deterministic for a fixed batch composition, but the serving runs batch differently from one another, so a delta of this size is expected. No accuracy regression. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Removes one `[num_tokens, moe_hidden_size]` bf16 copy per MoE layer per forward. MI355X, Kimi-K3, ROCm 7.2.4 / SGLang 0.5.20, `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1`, `bench_serving` random, single run per point: | ISL/OSL | Concurrency | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT strided (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s strided | Uplift | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1024/1024 | 4 | 18.57 | 18.20 | 207.9 | 212.0 | +2.0% | | 1024/1024 | 16 | 27.16 | 26.87 | 562.8 | 568.7 | +1.1% | | 1024/1024 | 64 | 45.88 | 45.29 | 1318.0 | 1335.2 | +1.3% | | 8192/1024 | 4 | 19.59 | 19.24 | 195.5 | 199.0 | +1.8% | | 8192/1024 | 16 | 32.03 | 31.73 | 463.3 | 467.7 | +0.9% | | 8192/1024 | 64 | 65.54 | 65.14 | 888.1 | 893.3 | +0.6% | The absolute TPOT saving sits at roughly 0.3–0.4 ms/token across every point (0.59 ms at 1024/64 is the one outlier), which is what a per-step saving proportional to layer count and near-flat in batch size should look like: the copy is small and latency-bound at decode batch sizes, so the relative uplift shrinks as concurrency grows and the step gets longer. TTFT moves by ≤0.6% in either direction on the 1024-token prefills and ≤0.1% on the 8192-token ones — noise. ### Traces One decode step (`step[DECODE bs=16]`) before and after, from the same region of the schedule: the merged front GEMM (`Cijk_Alik_Bljk_...MT32x16x1024...`) on the left, and `sglang::situ_and_mul_kernel` on the right. **Before** — an `at::native::elementwise_kernel_manual_unroll<128, 8, ...>` sits between them: that is the `.contiguous()` densifying the routed slice. **After** — the copy is gone and `situ_and_mul_kernel` follows the front GEMM directly. (The two screenshots are at different zoom levels, so the bar widths are not to a common scale — read them for kernel count and sequence, not for relative duration. The timing claims come from the table above.) ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #37341237759](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37341237759) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #37341237499](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37341237499) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #37341238089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37341238089)

files.patch:
@@ -142,6 +142,9 @@
 _is_hip = is_hip()
 _is_npu = is_npu()
 _aiter_k3_opt = get_bool_env_var("SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT")
+# A8W4 wins over AITER_SITUV2_A4W4 when both are set, matching aiter; with
+# neither, aiter's SiTU MoE runs a16w4 and takes bf16 activations.
+_aiter_situ_a8w4 = get_bool_env_var("AITER_SITUV2_A8W4", "false")
 
 
 def _cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
@@ -736,6 +739,8 @@ def _merge_front_weights(self) -> None:
             "_front_fp32",
             "_routing_contract_ok",
             "_ep_front_eligible",
+            # depends on _front_sizes, only known once the merge runs
+            "_aiter_takes_front_slice",
         ):
             self.__dict__.pop(prop, None)
 
@@ -1265,6 +1270,33 @@ def _moe_front_needs_dense_bf16(self) -> bool:
             and method.hidden_size == self.moe_hidden_size
         )
 
+    @cached_property
+    def _aiter_takes_front_slice(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether ROCm aiter reads the routed rows as the front GEMM hands them
+        over -- strided, no dense copy in between.
+
+        Only the A8W4 activation mode does: it quantizes through aiter's
+        fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort, and both kernels behind that entry
+        address rows via input.stride(-2), with only a same-shape view(-1, N) in
+        between. a16w4 re-densifies inside the FlyDSL stage1 port and A4W4 hands
+        the slice to a stage1 that takes no stride, so both keep the cast."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.mxfp4 import Mxfp4MoEMethod
+
+        method = self.experts.quant_method
+        if not (
+            _is_hip
+            and _aiter_situ_a8w4
+            and isinstance(method, Mxfp4MoEMethod)
+            and method.runner.runner_backend.is_aiter()
+            and method.hidden_size == self.moe_hidden_size
+            and self._front_sizes is not None
+        ):
+            return False
+        # aiter's fused_mx_quant_moe_sort_kernel vector-loads 16B from each row
+        # start, so the front row pitch and the slice's own base offset into it
+        # must both be 8 bf16 elems aligned.
+        return sum(self._front_sizes) % 8 == 0 and sum(self._front_sizes[:-1]) % 8 == 0
+
     @cached_property
     def _route_quant_fuse_eligible(self) -> bool:
         """Whether to stage routed_input for the fused route+pack+quant launch
@@ -1355,7 +1387,8 @@ def _forward_fused(
         )
         if num_tokens > 1 and _is_hip and not _aiter_k3_opt:
             router_logits = router_logits.contiguous()
-        if self._moe_front_needs_dense_bf16:
+        # False off ROCm, so this only ever widens the HIP path
+        if self._moe_front_needs_dense_bf16 and not self._aiter_takes_front_slice:
             # off an fp32 front the cast allocates the dense buffer, so the
             # contiguous() behind it is free; off a bf16 front it is the copy
             routed_input = routed_input.to(hidden_states.dtype).contiguous()
